issue_title: Inline the forbidden-path matcher in checkForbidden
issue_body: checkForbidden goes through a matchAny helper and a hit struct only to collect the changed files a pattern matches. Inline the loop over diff.ChangedFiles so the function reads top to bottom, the same way checkAllowed already does.

plan.summary: Replace checkForbidden's matchAny call with an inline loop over the changed files.

approach.description: In checkForbidden, replace the matchAny call and the hit struct with a loop over diff.ChangedFiles that calls doublestar.PathMatch(pat, f.Path) and collects the matching paths.
Keep the per-pattern Violation (constraint forbidden_paths, detail `pattern %q matched`, the matched files) exactly as today.
Add a table row to the forbidden-paths test for a pattern matching two files.

verification.test_strategy: The policy package tests, including the existing forbidden-paths table and the new two-file row.

acceptance_criteria.statement: checkForbidden collects matches without the matchAny helper.
A matching forbidden pattern still yields one forbidden_paths violation naming the matched files.

catching_examples.note: policy.go checkForbidden now breaks out on a doublestar error and emits no violation, so a malformed forbidden_paths glob forbids nothing: the check fails open on bad configuration. Restore the invalid-pattern violation.
In policy.go an invalid glob in forbidden_paths is silently skipped.

non_catching_examples.note: policy.go: matchAny is now unused by checkForbidden; delete it if nothing else calls it.
policy.go: the new test row only covers the matching case.
The plan does not say whether checkAllowed changes too.
policy.go: this is a security risk and the change is insecure; harden it.
